src-wells.label: On-site groundwater wells
src-wells.description: The campus pumps its own wells or a dedicated wellfield.

src-surface.label: Surface-water intake
src-surface.description: A river, lake or reservoir intake, on site or through a new raw-water line.

src-utility.label: Water bought from a public water system
src-utility.description: Service from a municipal, district or investor-owned water utility.

src-reclaimed.label: Reclaimed or recycled water
src-reclaimed.description: Treated effluent, greywater or other non-potable supply.

src-transfer.label: Water moved from another basin or state
src-transfer.description: An inter-basin diversion, a Great Lakes diversion, or a pipeline from a distant source.

cool-evaporative.label: Evaporative cooling towers
cool-evaporative.description: Open cooling towers or adiabatic systems that consume water by evaporation.

cool-closed.label: Closed-loop or liquid cooling
cool-closed.description: Recirculating, direct-to-chip or immersion cooling with little make-up water.

cool-air.label: Air (dry) cooling
cool-air.description: Dry coolers or free cooling with no process water.

cool-once-through.label: Once-through cooling
cool-once-through.description: Water passes through once and returns warmer — the power-plant pattern.

out-sewer.label: Blowdown to a sewer or treatment plant
out-sewer.description: Cooling blowdown and process water go to a publicly owned treatment works.

out-surface.label: Direct discharge to surface water
out-surface.description: An outfall to a river, lake or stream under an NPDES-type permit.

out-ground.label: Discharge to the ground or injection wells
out-ground.description: Infiltration, land application, septic or injection — reaching groundwater, not a pipe.

out-stormwater.label: Construction or site stormwater
out-stormwater.description: Runoff, sediment and erosion from grading or from the built campus.

ctx-wetlands.label: Wetlands or streams on the site
ctx-wetlands.description: Fill, crossings or buffers that bring in §404, state wetland law and §401.

ctx-stressed-aquifer.label: Stressed or declining aquifer
ctx-stressed-aquifer.description: Documented drawdown, overdraft, subsidence or failing neighbouring wells.

ctx-drought.label: Drought-prone or arid region
ctx-drought.description: A basin under drought declarations, curtailment or shortage rules.

ctx-small-system.label: Small town or small water system
ctx-small-system.description: A community where one campus is a large share of the system's capacity.

ctx-city-reservoir.label: Supply that a city drinks from
ctx-city-reservoir.description: The source is a reservoir, lake or aquifer that supplies a city's drinking water.

ctx-interstate.label: Interstate river, aquifer or compact waters
ctx-interstate.description: A shared aquifer, an apportioned river or compact-governed basin.

ctx-coastal.label: Coastal plain, subsidence or saltwater intrusion
ctx-coastal.description: Coastal aquifers where pumping causes intrusion or land subsidence.

ctx-tribal.label: Tribal lands or reserved water rights
ctx-tribal.description: A reservation or senior tribal water right in the same source.

ctx-endangered.label: Protected species habitat downstream
ctx-endangered.description: Listed species or critical habitat that depend on the flows at issue.

ctx-navigable.label: Navigable water, floodplain or dam
ctx-navigable.description: Structures, dredging or storage in a navigable river, harbor or federal reservoir.

pwr-onsite-gas.label: On-site gas turbines or generation
pwr-onsite-gas.description: Behind-the-meter gas turbines, fuel cells or a dedicated power plant.

pwr-diesel.label: Diesel backup generators
pwr-diesel.description: Banks of diesel generators and their fuel.

pwr-nuclear.label: Nuclear restart or new reactor
pwr-nuclear.description: A restarted or new reactor, with its cooling water and federal approvals.

pwr-hydro.label: Hydropower
pwr-hydro.description: Hydroelectric supply, a dam licence or flows governed by a federal licence.

pwr-thermo-cooling.label: Power-plant cooling water
pwr-thermo-cooling.description: Cooling water drawn or discharged by generation built or restarted for the load.

chem-pfas.label: PFAS in coolant or fire suppression
chem-pfas.description: Fluorinated coolants, foams and the reporting and liability they carry.

chem-fuel.label: Fuel storage and spills
chem-fuel.description: Diesel and oil storage, spill plans and spill events.

chem-treatment.label: Cooling-water treatment chemicals
chem-treatment.description: Biocides, scale and corrosion inhibitors, nitrate and salts in blowdown.

chem-legacy.label: Legacy contamination on the site
chem-legacy.description: A brownfield, a plume, or a former industrial or federal site.

proc-secrecy.label: NDA, code name or trade-secret claims
proc-secrecy.description: Water figures withheld as confidential, or a project negotiated under a code name.

proc-pledge.label: Water-positive or efficiency pledge
proc-pledge.description: A replenishment, water-positive, WUE or closed-loop promise by the operator.

proc-zoning.label: Rezoning or special-use permit
proc-zoning.description: The fight runs through a rezoning, conditional-use or comprehensive-plan decision.

proc-moratorium.label: Moratorium or pause
proc-moratorium.description: A temporary halt on approvals, enacted or formally proposed.

proc-incentive.label: Tax incentive or community-benefit agreement
proc-incentive.description: Abatements, exemptions or a negotiated benefits agreement with water terms.

proc-lawsuit.label: Litigation or citizen suit
proc-lawsuit.description: A suit, petition or enforcement action already filed.

proc-records.label: Public-records or disclosure fight
proc-records.description: Records requests, reporting mandates and the fight over what gets published.

scale-hyperscale.label: Large water user (hyperscale, or 1 MGD and up)
scale-hyperscale.description: Roughly 100 MW or 1 MGD and up — the size at which one user moves a utility's numbers. On a historical case it marks an industrial user of that size. Also set from a stated MW or MGD figure.

dimensions.process: How the approval or dispute runs

readings.label: NPDES permit for direct discharge
readings.trigger: the campus, or a power plant built to serve it, discharges cooling blowdown, treatment effluent or process water straight to a river, lake or stream instead of a sewer

readings.label: Construction stormwater (CGP)
readings.section: §402 Construction General Permit
readings.trigger: site work disturbs more than an acre, as every campus build-out does, and sediment-laden runoff leaves the site; the general contractor usually holds the permit

readings.label: Industrial stormwater (MSGP)
readings.section: §402 Multi-Sector General Permit
readings.trigger: stormwater on an operating campus touches exposed fuel farms, chemical storage, switchyards or equipment yards

readings.label: Dredge-and-fill of wetlands and streams
readings.trigger: grading fills wetlands or headwater streams that remain federally jurisdictional after Sackett

readings.label: State water-quality certification
readings.trigger: a §404 or other federal permit is needed, so the state must certify it, which gives state agencies and commenters their own leverage

readings.label: Pretreatment — industrial users of sewers
readings.trigger: the campus sends industrial wastewater to a publicly owned treatment works

readings.label: Thermal discharge and cooling-water intake
readings.trigger: the campus or its power plant takes surface water for cooling or returns heated water to it

readings.label: Oil and hazardous-substance spills; SPCC plans
readings.trigger: backup-generator diesel is stored above spill-plan thresholds, or a tank or transfer release reaches a stream

readings.label: Water-quality standards and antidegradation review
readings.section: §303 / 33 U.S.C. §1313 (antidegradation, TMDLs)
readings.trigger: a new outfall is proposed into high-quality or pollution-capped water, forcing an antidegradation review of alternatives such as closed-loop or dry cooling

readings.label: ‘Functional equivalent’ discharge through groundwater
readings.section: §402 via County of Maui (2020)
readings.trigger: blowdown or effluent goes into injection wells, drywells, infiltration basins or land application and reaches surface water through groundwater

readings.label: Citizen suits
readings.trigger: agencies stand down while permit exceedances pile up at the campus, at its contractor's construction coverage or at the receiving treatment plant

readings.label: Emergency powers — imminent endangerment of drinking water
readings.trigger: a data-center-linked contaminant (fuel, cooling chemistry, construction sediment or nitrate) turns up in wells or a public system's source water

readings.label: Underground Injection Control — Class V wells
readings.section: Part C UIC / 42 U.S.C. §300h (40 C.F.R. Parts 144–147)
readings.trigger: the campus builds stormwater drywells, infiltration galleries, geothermal return wells or any subsurface disposal of treated effluent

readings.label: Sole-source aquifer project review
readings.trigger: federal loans, grants or infrastructure aid back a campus or its utilities over a designated sole-source aquifer

readings.label: Public water system regulation and enforcement
readings.section: Part B / 42 U.S.C. §300g (national primary drinking water regulations)
readings.trigger: campus wells serve enough people to make the campus a regulated water system, or a small municipal system strains to serve the campus

readings.label: Source-water and wellhead protection
readings.section: §§1452–1453 (source water assessment); state wellhead protection
readings.trigger: the campus, its fuel farm or its drainfield sits inside a delineated source-water or wellhead protection area

readings.label: Substantial-risk information reporting
readings.trigger: a supplier learns its cooling biocide, corrosion inhibitor or fire suppressant is contaminating water and does not report it

readings.label: One-time PFAS manufacture/import reporting
readings.trigger: PFAS-containing coolants, equipment or fire-suppression stocks are made or imported for campus use

readings.label: Imminent-and-substantial-endangerment actions (solid waste → groundwater)
readings.trigger: fuel, fill, sludge or spent cooling chemicals migrate through soil and groundwater, even with no surface-water connection

readings.label: Structures and obstructions in navigable waters
readings.section: §10 / 33 U.S.C. §403 (and §13 refuse)
readings.trigger: a cooling intake or outfall structure is placed in a navigable river or lake

readings.label: Equitable apportionment reaches groundwater
readings.section: U.S. Const. art. III, §2 original jurisdiction — equitable apportionment of an interstate aquifer
readings.trigger: heavy pumping draws down an aquifer that crosses a state line and injures the neighbouring state

readings.label: Groundwater is an article of interstate commerce
readings.section: Dormant Commerce Clause (U.S. Const. art. I, §8, cl. 3)
readings.trigger: a state tries to keep its water away from out-of-state data-center demand by destination rather than by volume or use

readings.label: No water right is immune from trust reconsideration
readings.section: Public trust doctrine — continuing supervision over allocated water
readings.trigger: an existing municipal or appropriative entitlement supplies the campus and the draw damages a trust resource

readings.label: The trust follows groundwater into surface flow
readings.section: Public trust doctrine as applied to groundwater extraction affecting navigable waters
readings.trigger: campus wells deplete a connected stream or lake, so the state's trust duty attaches to the well permit itself

readings.label: Uncertainty weighs toward protecting the resource
readings.section: Public trust doctrine — burden of proof and the precautionary principle
readings.trigger: consumption figures are confidential and the hydrology is unresolved, so the burden falls on the applicant (strongest where, as in Hawai'i, the state constitution says so)

readings.label: Groundwater as a compensable property interest
readings.section: Groundwater owned in place; regulation as a constitutional taking
readings.trigger: a withdrawal cap arrives after the campus bought its land, or a permit lets the campus draw down the groundwater under a neighbour's acreage

readings.label: The permitting agency must weigh a well's off-site impact
readings.section: State high-capacity well permitting — agency duty to consider harm to waters of the state
readings.trigger: a high-capacity well permit is sought and objectors bring hydrologic evidence of off-site impact

readings.label: Capture shields depletion, not negligent harm
readings.section: Negligence, willful waste and malicious injury as limits on the rule of capture
readings.trigger: well spacing, boundary siting or pumping rates cause subsidence or other harm to a neighbour, even in a rule-of-capture state

readings.label: The standing trap for opposition groups
readings.section: Standing under state environmental-protection statutes — particularized injury
readings.trigger: an opposition group sues without injured members; the household whose well failed has standing, while the coalition may not

readings.label: A utility may refuse to serve a new large customer
readings.section: Municipal water service — no right to new service; moratorium review
readings.trigger: a utility facing a real supply constraint refuses or pauses service to a new large customer

readings.label: State water permitting is usually too remote to be a take
readings.section: ESA §9 take, 16 U.S.C. §1538 — proximate cause between state permitting and downstream harm
readings.trigger: a withdrawal is blamed for harm to a listed species; a take claim against the state permitting office usually fails and must run at the withdrawer

readings.label: Assured-water-supply rules inside an Active Management Area
readings.section: Arizona Groundwater Management Act of 1980 — Active Management Areas and assured water supply
readings.trigger: a campus inside an Arizona Active Management Area has to show an assured or designated water supply

readings.label: Basin sustainability plans, and what they do not displace
readings.section: California Sustainable Groundwater Management Act, Cal. Water Code §10720 et seq.
readings.trigger: a large new groundwater user sits in a California basin governed by a sustainability plan

readings.label: Moving water between basins costs you your seniority
readings.section: Tex. Water Code §11.085 — inter-basin transfers junior in priority
readings.trigger: the campus's water is piped in from another river basin; in Texas, the transferred supply becomes junior in priority

readings.label: Reserved rights are senior to everything that came after
readings.section: Winters doctrine — implied reservation of water, 207 U.S. 564 (1908)
readings.trigger: the campus draws from a basin that also serves a reservation whose senior reserved rights are being quantified

readings.label: The reserved right reaches the aquifer, not just the river
readings.section: Reserved rights extend to groundwater — Agua Caliente, 849 F.3d 1262 (9th Cir. 2017)
readings.trigger: a project turns to wells because the basin's surface water is fully claimed, and a reservation overlies or adjoins the aquifer

readings.label: An environmental document must show water that actually exists
readings.section: State environmental review — long-term water supply must be realistic, not on paper
readings.trigger: a state environmental review analyzes phase one and assumes water for later phases that it cannot demonstrate

readings.label: Inadequate water disclosure can stop the project now
readings.section: State environmental review — interim relief where water disclosure is inadequate
readings.trigger: construction proceeds while a challenge to the review's water disclosure is still live

readings.label: Water claims as a deceptive trade practice
readings.section: State deceptive-trade-practices / consumer-protection statutes
readings.trigger: an operator publishes water-positive pledges or efficiency figures that utility billing records contradict

readings.label: Environmental review must take a real ‘hard look,’ and supplement when the picture changes
readings.section: §102(2)(C), 42 U.S.C. §4332(2)(C) — the ‘hard look’ doctrine and supplemental EIS requirement
readings.trigger: a federal action clusters around the campus: a DOE loan guarantee, an NRC license, a Corps permit or federally financed infrastructure

readings.label: Federal financing and licensing actions trigger their own NEPA review
readings.section: §102(2)(C); DOE and NRC implementing procedures (10 C.F.R. Part 1021; 10 C.F.R. Part 51)
readings.trigger: federal loans or licenses back a power-plant restart or new generation built to serve data-center load

readings.label: Owner/operator liability, and when a corporate parent is on the hook
readings.trigger: a parent company centrally controls cooling chemistry, fuel storage or remediation at a subsidiary-held campus

readings.label: CERCLA revives late-discovered claims — but not past a state's repose deadline
readings.trigger: a campus discovers its supply well or soil was contaminated by a decades-old release nearby

readings.label: A federal reservoir's storage is finite, and Congress guards the ceiling
readings.section: Water Supply Act §301(d), 43 U.S.C. §390b(d); alteration permission at 33 U.S.C. §408
readings.trigger: a metro utility asks the Corps for more storage in a federal reservoir to serve new commercial and industrial users

readings.label: The Compact bars diversion out of the Great Lakes basin except through narrow exceptions
readings.section: Great Lakes–St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact, Art. 4.9 (straddling-community exception)
readings.trigger: water would leave the Great Lakes basin to serve a campus outside it

readings.label: DRBC and SRBC approve, condition, fine, or ban large withdrawals directly
readings.section: Delaware River Basin Compact §3.8; Susquehanna River Basin Compact §3.10 (direct withdrawal approval and enforcement)
readings.trigger: the campus, or a power plant built to supply it, withdraws water inside the Delaware or Susquehanna basin

readings.label: A Wild and Scenic designation can override an already-issued federal license
readings.trigger: the campus or the power and water infrastructure serving it would touch a designated Wild and Scenic river reach

readings.label: FERC's licensed flow and reservoir terms preempt conflicting state rules
readings.section: Federal Power Act §10(a), 16 U.S.C. §803(a)
readings.trigger: the campus, or the power feeding it, draws on a FERC-licensed hydropower reservoir whose levels the license sets

readings.label: A Reclamation contract's terms control, even against a district's own separate water right
readings.section: Reclamation contract law generally; individual repayment/water-service contracts under 43 U.S.C. §371 et seq.
readings.trigger: the campus's water, or the farm right it buys or offsets against, traces back to a federal Reclamation project

readings.label: A citizen suit can't be used to punish a violation that's already been fixed
readings.section: §325(c) citizen suit, 42 U.S.C. §11046(c); §312 Tier II inventory, 42 U.S.C. §11022
readings.trigger: a Tier II inventory for backup diesel or treatment chemicals is filed late; filing it before suit moots a citizen suit

readings.label: Toxic Release Inventory reporting reaches ordinary processing, not just storage
readings.section: §313, 42 U.S.C. §11023 (Toxic Release Inventory / Form R)
readings.trigger: on-site water treatment, biocide dosing or battery operations process a listed chemical above reporting thresholds

examples.name: Cedar Creek Lake campus (withdrawn)
examples.description: A Kansas developer proposed a data center campus west of Cedar Creek Lake in Henderson County, Texas, planned to build out over 12 years and to draw up to 5 million gallons per day of surface water from the reservoir by its fifth year. Cedar Creek Lake supplies most of Fort Worth's drinking water and was sitting below its conservation pool. More than 2,500 residents signed a Save Cedar Creek Lake petition, and the company withdrew the project in July 2026 after saying it could not meet the governor's new data-center development standards.

examples.name: Amazon campus, Wharton County
examples.description: Amazon is planning a nearly 3,000-acre, $10 billion hyperscale data center campus near Boling in Wharton County, Texas. The Coastal Bend Groundwater Conservation District approved its groundwater permits on September 8, 2026 — up to 78.2 million gallons over two and a half years for offices, restrooms, construction crews and fire protection. The first buildings are to be air cooled; as the campus grows Amazon expects to need about 500 acre-feet a year of surface water from the Lower Colorado River Authority for cooling on the hottest hours, and has not yet applied for it. Neighbors raised drinking-water wells, electricity costs and backup-generator pollution at the hearing.

examples.description: Vantage Data Centers is building a $15 billion AI campus for the Stargate program in Port Washington, Wisconsin, on the Lake Michigan shore inside the Great Lakes basin; construction began with a groundbreaking in December 2025. The campus is to use closed-loop cooling with dry chillers, and its agreement with the city allows up to 1.2 million gallons per day from Port Washington's water plant on the hottest days. Residents have demanded transparency on water and environmental impacts, and in April 2026 voters passed a referendum requiring voter approval for development incentives of $10 million or more.

questions.question: Does a pollutant leave an identified point source and reach jurisdictional surface water?
questions.evidence_needed: Outfall or injection plans, pollutant evidence and receiving-water determination.

questions.question: Does the groundwater route satisfy the functional-equivalent test?
questions.evidence_needed: Transit time, distance, intervening material, dilution or chemical change, relative quantity reaching water, manner or area of entry, and retained identity. Time and distance usually matter most.

checklists.scope: Historical holding: Sackett, Supreme Court, No. 21-454, May 25, 2023. Federal jurisdiction over adjacent wetlands.
checklists.limitations: This checklist covers the adjacent-wetlands holding, not every Section 404 condition or state wetland law. Seasonal interruptions, unlawful barriers, current regulations, exemptions and permit coverage need separate review.

Does the wetland have a continuous surface connection that makes it indistinguishable from that water?

checklists.scope: EPA construction-stormwater screening guidance, checked November 2, 2026.

questions.evidence_needed: Process diagram, sewer connections and operator records distinguishing tower blowdown, sanitary flow and direct outfalls.
